blocks.text: Acreage and rural land in Fraser Valley

items.t: ALR vs non-ALR is the first split in every valley acreage trade: The structural profile that is sourced: acreage housing in the ALR is freehold in practice and single-residence-led — one principal residence (≤500 m²) plus at most one additional residence (90 m² / 186 m² by parcel size), a secondary suite only inside the principal residence, and no stratification without ALC permission — so the multi-unit strata profile of urban pages does not exist on ALR parcels.

Serviced vs unserviced is the second split: Built urban-fringe parcels sit on municipal water and sewer under their city's or township's servicing bylaw; rural and FVRD parcels trade on well and septic, with water licences and irrigation rights as separate parcel facts.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect acreage buyers in Fraser Valley

items.t: In Abbotsford (for comparison only): the current Official Community Plan is Abbotsforward 2050. It doesn't apply to properties in the Township of Langley, Surrey, Mission or the Fraser Valley Regional District's rural areas.

Mission and the regional district each have their own rules. City of Mission: OCP Bylaw 6405-2026 (adopted June 1, 2026), Zoning Bylaw 5949-2020, small-scale housing Bylaw 6299-2024 and development servicing Bylaw 5650-2017, with a flat 10% tax penalty after July 2 and no Supreme Court registry. Rural Fraser Valley Regional District land: taxes are due July 2, with 5% added on amounts unpaid then and another 5% on amounts unpaid October 31, billed by the Surveyor of Taxes and paid to the Province. Which rules apply depends on the parcel's jurisdiction, not its mailing address or real estate board area.

blocks.text: Good to know about Fraser Valley

items.t: There's no market figure for acreages: every city figure you see next to an acreage listing is a housing figure (detached, or condos and townhomes combined) that includes acreages without measuring them. Price an acreage parcel by parcel, using its own area's sales, its ALR status, water, buildings and farm income; it's the only reliable way.
The rule people most often get wrong: ALR land "cannot be stratified without the Agricultural Land Commission's permission". It's a permission rule, not an outright ban.

Servicing numbers do not transfer between jurisdictions: a buyer comparing a Township parcel (Bylaw 5382) with an FVRD parcel and a Chilliwack parcel (candidate 3055, not adopted) is looking at three different positions, not three comparable numbers — for the second and third the honest answer is the process, and Mission's or Chilliwack's numbers should not be applied to FVRD ground.

faq.a: Generally one principal residence (maximum 500 m² total floor area), plus, where the property qualifies, one additional residence capped at 90 m² on parcels of 40 ha or less or 186 m² on parcels over 40 ha; more than that, or a larger residence, requires ALC approval, and local bylaws may restrict further.
faq.q: How many homes can I have on an ALR acreage?

faq.a: BC Assessment's minimum gross farm income (farm gate) thresholds are $2,500 for an operation of 0.8 ha to 4 ha, $2,500 plus 5% of the actual value of the area over 4 ha for a larger operation, and $10,000 for an operation under 0.8 ha; new applications are due by the legislated October 31 deadline.
faq.q: What farm income does an acreage need to keep farm classification?

faq.a: Many do. Ask for the well flow test and water quality results, and the septic filing and inspection records, before you remove conditions.
faq.q: Do acreages in Fraser Valley have wells and septic?

faq.a: It depends on the zoning, whether the land is in the Agricultural Land Reserve, servicing and the minimum lot size, and it needs municipal approval. Ask the municipality before you buy with a subdivision in mind.
